summary: We searched the news for each contest district and compared the polls we found with VoteHub. Polls VoteHub lacks were added by hand (data/polls_manual.csv) and weighted like every other poll. Effect on our answers: NC-01 0.88 → 0.84, OH-07 0.88 → 0.83, PA-08 0.88 → 0.88, NY-17 0.66 → 0.65, NC-11 unchanged at 0.88.

items: New, more Republican lines since 2025. Incumbent Don Davis (D) against Laurie Buckhout (R).
Added: RedBox Research (D) of 23 Oct, Davis 45–44; GQR (D) of 29 Sep – 4 Oct, 47–39; GBAO for House Majority PAC (D) of 9–11 Sep, 50–43.
Not added: a co/efficient (R) poll of 6–8 Oct that one tracker reports as Buckhout 43–42 and another as a generic ballot.
Inside Elections moved the race toward Democrats; RealClearPolitics calls it a toss-up.
Chuck Edwards (R) withdrew in August after a House Ethics Committee report. The party picked state Rep. Jennifer Balkcom; Trump endorsed her.
Jamie Ager (D) raised $2.3 million in the third quarter against $0.36 million for Balkcom.
The only poll of the real matchup is Emerson (12–14 Oct), Ager 56–43, already in our data. RedBox tested Ager against a generic Republican and is not used.
This explains the gap between DDHQ's 22 Oct probability (0.52) and the markets (0.85).
Incumbent Max Miller (R) against Brian Poindexter (D). No independent poll since August.
Added: RedBox Research (D) of 23 Oct, Poindexter 46–42; co/efficient (R) of 6 Aug, 47–33; GBAO (D) of 20 Jun, Miller 44–43. The newest poll now carries most of the weight, so our poll average fell.
DDHQ's live model moved to 51% Poindexter on 27 Oct (we use its 22 Oct value, 0.48). Inside Elections rates it a toss-up.
Incumbent Rob Bresnahan (R) against Scranton mayor Paige Cognetti (D).
Added: The New York Times/Siena College (402 likely voters, released 25 Oct), Cognetti 51–46, the only independent high-quality poll in any contest district; RedBox Research (D) of 23 Oct, 49–46.
Cook rates it a toss-up; PredictIt has no tight quote.
Incumbent Mike Lawler (R) against Cait Conley (D). The second and last debate was described as a dead heat.
Added: McLaughlin & Associates for the Lawler campaign (28–30 Sep), Lawler 50–47; RedBox Research (D) of 23 Oct, Conley 48–46. Emerson (27–29 Sep, Conley 48–46) was already in.
Cook and The New York Times list it among about 18 toss-ups.
